what: Emerson Electric sells industrial automation. It supplies the control systems, valves, measurement instruments and software that run refineries, chemical plants, power stations and factories, and it owns most of the engineering software firm Aspen Technology.
customers: Process industries such as oil, gas, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, plus discrete manufacturers and power producers.
money: valves, regulators, sensors and analytical instruments
distributed control systems and industrial software including AspenTech
moat: Control systems that run a plant for twenty years and are replaced only during rare shutdowns, which gives it long service and upgrade revenue.
risks: Capital spending by oil, gas and chemical customers is cyclical
Growth has been modest at about 5% a year
Acquiring the rest of AspenTech used significant capital
Industrial demand in China and Europe has been soft
opportunities: Plant operators are investing in automation software to cut labour and energy costs
Its software business carries far higher margins than hardware
Liquefied natural gas and power projects are a large source of new orders
watch: Underlying orders growth, which leads revenue by two to three quarters.
